PC-PTSD-5 PTSD Screen — FHIR Questionnaire Template

Short primary care screen for probable PTSD after a traumatic event, with an automatic score and positive-screen flag.

Open in Builder

Scoring

Each Yes to the follow-up questions scores 1; they are asked only after a reported traumatic event, and no event scores 0. The score (0–5) is a positive screen at 4 or more.

Questions

  1. Have you ever experienced this kind of event?
    • Yes
    • No
  2. Had nightmares about the event(s) or thought about the event(s) when you did not want to?
    • Yes
    • No
  3. Tried hard not to think about the event(s) or went out of your way to avoid situations that reminded you of the event(s)?
    • Yes
    • No
  4. Been constantly on guard, watchful, or easily startled?
    • Yes
    • No
  5. Felt numb or detached from people, activities, or your surroundings?
    • Yes
    • No
  6. Felt guilty or unable to stop blaming yourself or others for the event(s) or any problems the event(s) may have caused?
    • Yes
    • No

Calculated results

  • PC-PTSD-5 score (0–5)
  • Screening result

Source and license

Source: Prins et al. 2015, Primary Care PTSD Screen for DSM-5 (PC-PTSD-5), VA National Center for PTSD. Codes: LOINC. (link)

License: Developed by staff at VA's National Center for PTSD; in the public domain and not copyrighted. Intended for use by qualified health professionals and researchers. (link)

Provided to save authoring effort, not as medical advice — confirm the scale and its cut-offs for your use case.

Use it

  1. Download the FHIR Questionnaire JSON, or
  2. open it in the Builder right away (or open the Builder, choose + Add → From template… and search for “PC-PTSD-5 PTSD Screen”). It arrives as one titled group with its calculations wired, and you can keep editing it.
